definitions.explanation: The act of shaking hands as a greeting or sign of agreement.

examples.japanese: {握手|あくしゅ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦しましょう→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{初|はじ}めて→初めて：02932_hajimete⟧⟦{会|あ}った→会う：00482_au⟧⟦{時|とき}→時：02918_toki⟧、{握手|あくしゅ}⟦しました→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: We shook hands when we first met.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{握手|あくしゅ}⟦できて→できる：00557_dekiru⟧⟦{嬉|うれ}しかったです→嬉しい：00822_ureshii⟧。
examples.english: I was happy to shake hands with him.

examples.japanese: ⟦{契約|けいやく}→契約：02698_keiyaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{成立|せいりつ}した→成立：04353_seiritsu⟧ので、{握手|あくしゅ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{交|か}わしました→交わす：noentry⟧。
examples.english: Since the contract was finalized, we exchanged handshakes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{強|つよ}く→強い：00820_tsuyoi⟧{握手|あくしゅ}⟦されて→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{痛|いた}かった→痛い：01108_itai⟧。
examples.english: It hurt when they shook my hand firmly.

notes:
{握手|あくしゅ} means handshake.

TRANSITIVITY (as suru verb):
- Type: {自動詞|じどうし}
- Pattern: Xと{握手|あくしゅ}する (shake hands with X)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {握手|あくしゅ}をする (shake hands)
- ～と{握手|あくしゅ}する (shake hands with ~)
- {握手|あくしゅ}を{求|もと}める (ask for a handshake)
- {握手|あくしゅ}{会|かい} (meet-and-greet, handshake event)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Handshaking is less common in traditional Japanese culture (bowing is standard), but is used in business and international contexts.
